reasons: The cited paragraph (p0054) genuinely deviates from the rule: the Deliverable licence is 'revocable, non-transferable', limited to the Order Form term, and omits Affiliates and contractors — squarely at the stated walk-away line despite the compliant grant in Sections 13.1–13.3, so flagging 14.2 as a deviation is correct.

The redline applies only rule-scoped fixes (delete 'revocable' and 'non-transferable', make the paid-up licence perpetual/irrevocable, extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf, add Affiliate/successor transfer keyed to Section 13.3) and leaves Vendor's ownership sentence and the 'use a Deliverable' scope intact — directionally correct for the customer and rule-complete.

The two failed minimal-edit checks (0.78/0.85 changed-character ratio) are explained by the paragraph's brevity: nearly every element of the one-sentence grant (revocability, transferability, term, licensee scope) is what the rule requires changing, so the high ratio reflects density rather than scope creep; no extraneous obligations were introduced.

Comment is compliant with tone requirements: prefixed, first-person plural, two sentences explaining the change and citing the playbook position, and it offers the fallback (Affiliates on written notice, transfer limited to an M&A successor). Minor nit only: it cites 'Sections 13.2–13.3' while the rationale cites 13.1–13.3 — worth aligning but not disqualifying.
